downgrade-overage-01.graded_text: A stable, deterministic order (such as oldest first) decides which 25 books stay covered. Books beyond that keep all their data, are refused gated operations with a clear product message rather than deleted, and become covered again as soon as the plan or freed capacity allows.

votes.e: docs/downgrade-policy.md L23: "A book is **covered** when it is among the 25 oldest active (not in Trash) books by creation time. The rest are **frozen**." L75: "coverage is computed from the current plan and the account's active books ordered by `(createdAt, id)` ... The id tiebreak keeps the order stable". Data kept: L7 "Nothing is deleted, locked, or rewritten because a plan ended"; refusal with product message: L83 `book_frozen`, L95-96 "typed outcome codes, turned into product copy ... A frozen book opens with its editing controls replaced by a short read-only note". Re-covered: L37 "Trashing a covered book makes the oldest frozen book covered"; L61 "All 40 books editable again at once".

downgrade-overage-02.graded_text: The policy states an explicit rule for the account above the 1.5 GB total: no book or photo is deleted by the system, existing photos stay at least readable, the user can remove any photo either on its own or by deleting the book that holds it, and storage cannot keep growing past the Free allowance while the account is over it.

votes.e: docs/downgrade-policy.md No deletion: L7 "Nothing is deleted, locked, or rewritten because a plan ended"; L60 "Data lost | None." Readable: L44 "A photo stored under Pro (up to 120 MB) keeps working wherever it already is: it renders, exports, prints". Removal: L19 storage limit never touches "Anything that keeps or removes bytes"; L30 frozen books allow "Move to Trash, restore from Trash, delete permanently | Yes | Yes"; L48 "Deleting from Trash permanently, or waiting for the purge, does [free space]" (individual photo removal only in covered books, see blocking). No growth: L48 "While usage plus the size of an incoming upload is more than 1.5 GB, the upload is refused"; L36 duplicate needs "storage room for the copy".

downgrade-overage-03.graded_text: The policy states an explicit rule for existing photos above the new 40 MB single-photo limit: they are kept and stay readable, with no compression, resizing, or deletion, and new uploads must meet the 40 MB limit.

downgrade-overage-04.graded_text: Bytes held in Trash count toward the total storage allowance during the downgrade.

votes.e: docs/downgrade-policy.md L48: "Usage is the total size of every stored photo, **including photos in Trash**"; L38: "their bytes count toward storage until they are purged"; L57 typical case uses 2.6 GB including Trash.

downgrade-overage-05.graded_text: Coverage and limits are derived from the current plan when a request arrives and enforced on the server for the browser app, the API, and the MCP connection alike, rather than kept as a lock flag stamped on each book.

votes.e: docs/downgrade-policy.md L11: "No job runs at that moment and no record is touched: every gate reads the current plan on each request"; L75: "There is no `locked`, `frozen`, or `overLimit` column and no job that sets one. On each check, coverage is computed from the current plan"; L79: "All three checks live in the domain package and run inside the backend mutations. The browser app, public API, MCP server, and background jobs all go through those mutations".

downgrade-overage-06.graded_text: A cancelled account cannot create a book while it holds 25 or more books.

votes.e: docs/downgrade-policy.md L36: "**Creating or duplicating a book** needs fewer than 25 active books"; L84 `assertCanAddBook(account)` on "Create, duplicate" refuses `book_limit_reached`; L56: "No new books until they have 24 or fewer active books."

blocking: [claude-fallback] docs/downgrade-policy.md L89: "the size and storage check runs when the client asks for upload permission, before any bytes move ... Usage is recorded when the upload is finalized." Outstanding grants are not reserved against usage, so several concurrent or sequential permission requests each see the same un-incremented usage and all pass; an account at 1.4 GB can be granted many uploads and finish well past 1.5 GB. Nothing says the signed grant pins content-length or that finalize re-checks the real object size, so a hostile client can declare a small size and upload up to whatever the bucket allows, which breaks both the 40 MB and 1.5 GB limits.

[claude-fallback] docs/downgrade-policy.md L36/L84: "needs fewer than 25 active books" via `assertCanAddBook` with no transaction, lock, or uniqueness guard named. Two concurrent creates at 24 active books both pass the count check and the account ends at 26. The same unguarded check-then-act applies to duplicate.

[claude-fallback] docs/downgrade-policy.md L7 promises Losing Pro "never takes away the ability to see, export, print, or clean up what the user already made", but L31-32 forbid photo edits and replacement in frozen books, and L83 runs `assertBookEditable` on "Every mutation that changes a book's content". So an over-storage user can't remove one oversized photo from a frozen book. Their only way to reclaim space there is to trash and permanently delete the whole book, which contradicts the stated principle. In the typical case the newest 15 books, likely holding the Pro-era 60-110 MB photos, are exactly the frozen ones.
